subject: Dedicated adoption: technical checklist, gap list & next steps
messages:
From: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.com>
To: Alex Cheng <alex.cheng@finteq.com>, Priya Rao <priya@finteq.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@sean.gallagher@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-04-22T09:05:00-07:00
Subject: Dedicated adoption: technical checklist, gap list & next steps

Alex / Priya — thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap and the technical checklist we promised attached (redwood-dedicated-checklist.xlsx). High level takeaways:

- Goal: transition Finteq's search and document ingestion pipelines to Redwood Dedicated for routing-sensitive workloads and to reduce token cost for embeddings/reranking.
- Priority features: private VPC, KMS integration, streaming + structured tool-calling for document summarization, and a reranking pipeline that uses generation + embedding score fusion.
- Constraints: peak concurrent inference for embeddings/rerank expected ~1,200 qps during market open windows; typical baseline 150 qps. Latency SLO for user-facing rerank step is <= 350ms p95.

Open technical questions (we need your answers to finalize sizing):
1) Auth: do you require customer-managed HSM-backed KMS or is cloud-managed KMS sufficient? (We can support both; HSM adds procurement steps.)
2) Network: will the Dedicated nodes be in Finteq VPC (preferred) or do you want Redwood to host in a private peered VPC?
3) SDK / routing: do you expect to use our SDK with in-app routing by customer-id, or will you route through an internal proxy that assigns tenant headers?
4) Tool-calling / structured output: sample schema for the summarizer? We can enforce strict JSON schema on the model output to avoid parsing errors.
5) Reranker: do you want generation-based candidate expansion (costly) or strictly embedding-based reranking with a smaller generator for context?

Next steps (proposed):
- Finteq provides answers to Q1–Q4 by EOD Friday (2027-04-23).
- Redwood will produce a draft autoscale/concurrency plan + queueing model and a cost estimate by Tuesday (2027-04-27).
- Legal / procurement kickoff: we'll introduce the MA template; procurement@finteq to confirm timelines.

I've attached an initial gap list row in the sheet for the items we covered. Ben / Marissa / Sean — please add sizing assumptions to the "Ops Sizing" tab and highlight any blockers before EOD Monday.

Thanks,
Mina
Mina Haddad
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
(attachment: redwood-dedicated-checklist.xlsx)

From: Alex Cheng <alex.cheng@finteq.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.com>
Cc: Priya Rao <priya@finteq.com>
Date: 2027-04-22T11:26:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated adoption: technical checklist, gap list & next steps

Mina — thank you, very clear. A few quick clarifications inline: 

- KMS: we need HSM-backed keys (regulatory). We'll need a short questionnaire for security to review HSM configuration.
- Network: we prefer Redwood to deploy Dedicated into our AWS account (Finteq VPC) and we'll provide a dedicated subnet and peering.
- SDK / routing: we'll run an internal proxy layer that annotates requests with finteq-customer-id and priority class; we'd like the SDK to be used for model orchestration only.
- Tool-calling/structured output: attaching the summarizer output schema (see small excerpt below). We need strict JSON schema enforcement for the invoice extraction flow.

Also — the 1,200 qps is worst-case for embeddings during market open; that is for short embedding vectors (512 dims) across 4k daily concurrent flows. Average will be much lower. We can try to provide historical qps charts before Friday.

I'll loop procurement on timeline.

Best,
Alex

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-04-22T16:12:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated adoption: technical checklist, gap list & next steps

Adding initial ops sizing notes against Mina's checklist — quick points: 

- Baseline assumptions I used (will add to sheet): embedding model small-quant (8-bit) ~ 8ms/token at 32 batch on A100-class nodes; generator for candidate expansion 1.2x cost of embedding call.
- Autoscale: recommend two-tier queueing:
  * Inference hot path (user-facing rerank + tool-call): reserved concurrency pool -> p95 <= 350ms target.
  * Batch embedding pipeline (ingestion / periodic re-rank): background queue with prefetching and spot-capacity burst.
- Concurrency: set soft concurrency limit per GPU to 48 small-embedding requests and hard cap at 64 with backpressure at 56. These numbers will change if Finteq provides histogram of sequence lengths.
- Fallbacks: configure routing policy that falls back to cheaper open-quant model if dedicated pool is saturated (best-effort, increased latency).

I'll populate "Ops Sizing" tab with computed node counts for the 150 qps baseline and the 1,200 qps peak. Expecting to need ~8 reserved gpus for baseline and ~54 GPUs for peak if using same model profile; we should discuss quantization tradeoffs to reduce peak nodes.

Note: need Priya / Finteq to confirm allowed BLAST windows for pre-warming and whether scheduled bursts are acceptable.

-b
Ben Carter
Principal Solutions Architect | Redwood Inference
(attachment: ma-template-v1.docx)

From: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.com>
To: Alex Cheng <alex.cheng@finteq.com>, Priya Rao <priya@finteq.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>, procurement@finteq.com
Date: 2027-04-23T14:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated adoption: technical checklist, gap list & next steps — actions confirmed

Alex / Priya — thanks for the quick follow. Confirming next steps and owners: 

1) Finteq to confirm KMS/HSM timeline and provide security questionnaire responses — owner: Priya (due 2027-04-23 EOD).
2) Finteq to share historical qps + sequence length histograms for embeddings (CSV) — owner: Alex (due 2027-04-23 EOD).
3) Redwood will deliver draft autoscale + queueing model + cost delta for quantization options — owner: Ben (deliver by 2027-04-27).
4) Redwood legal to send MA template and track procurement conversation — owner: Marissa (intro to procurement@finteq.com by 2027-04-24).
5) Technical deep-dive session (30–45m) to walk inference paths (tool-calls, structured schema enforcement, reranker fusion) — proposed slot: 2027-04-28 10:00am PT. Ben / Sean to lead.

If we get the qps CSV today we can run a quick simulation and likely trim the peak node count by adopting mixed-quant models. Please add any missing items to the checklist sheet and I'll update the deal plan in HubSpot once we have confirmations.

Thanks,
Mina
Mina Haddad
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
